title: Comparative Analysis of Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning Regression Models for Codon-Level k-mer Composition Analysis of the Nipah Virus Genome
abstract: Abstract The Nipah virus (NiV) is highly virulent zoonotic paramyxovirus, where a complete genome sequence resource is relatively limited compared to other emerging pathogens. In this study, the codon level (3-mer) k-mer composition analysis of 93 complete Nipah virus genome sequences retrieved from the NCBI Nucleotide database was presented. The genomes were encoded into a vector of 64 elements representing the number of appearances of each of the 64 three-nucleotide combinations. The feature set was subjected to descriptive statistics, covariance and Pearson correlation between each feature, which showed very high degrees of pairwise collinearity in the set of codon-count features. Using a correlation-based feature-selection procedure (|r| > 0.99), the feature space was reduced from 64 to 5 almost independent codon counts (AAA, TAG, TCG, CGC and CCG). We considered seven regression algorithms across three learning paradigms (classical models: Linear Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine/SVR, an ensemble model: Random Forest, deep sequential models: Long Short-Term Memory network and Simple Recurrent Neural Network, and a Decision Tree baseline) and compared their performance using the number of codons CCG as a regression target and the remaining four codon counts as predictors. The 70/20/10 train/validation/test split was used to train all models, and they were compared using the coefficient of determination (R2), root mean squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Decision Tree Regression achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.9945), followed by Linear Regression (R2 = 0.9908), Random Forest (R2 = 0.9892), LSTM (R2 = 0.9731), and SimpleRNN (R2 = 0.9718), while KNN (R2 = 0.8038) and SVM/SVR (R2 = 0.1038 with feature scaling) underperformed. The results are evaluated with the knowledge of the large compositional constraints on codon usage over a set of Nipah virus genomes, the known sensitivity of instance- and margin-based regressors to unscaled, collinear small-sample data, and the limited benefit of deep sequential architectures on a pseudo-sequence of a very small tabular sample (no temporal dimension). This paper presents in a transparent manner the pipeline results, statistical results and comparative modeling results, along with the limitations of the dataset, as a baseline for future codon-composition based computational studies of Nipah virus.

abstract_zh: 摘要 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒)是一种高度致病性的动物源性副粘病毒,与其他新兴病原体相比,其完整的基因组序列资源相对有限。本研究展示了从NCBI核苷酸数据库中检索到的93条完整的尼帕病毒 基因组序列的编码子(3-mer)水平的k-mer组成分析。基因组被编码为一个包含64个元素的媒介,每个元素代表64种三核苷酸组合的出现次数。对特征集进行了描述性统计分析,并计算了各特征之间的协方差和皮尔逊相关系数,结果显示该编码子计数特征集内部存在极高的成对共线性。通过基于相关性的特征选择过程(|r| > 0.99),将特征空间从64个减少到几乎独立的5个编码子计数(AAA、TAG、TCG、CGC和CCG)。我们考虑了七种回归算法,涵盖三种学习范式(经典模型:线性回归、K近邻、支持向量机/支持向量回归;集成模型:随机森林;深度序列模型:长短期记忆网络和简单循环神经网络;以及决策树基线模型),并以编码子CCG的数量作为回归目标,其余四个编码子计数作为预测变量进行比较。所有模型均采用70/20/10的训练/验证/测试划分方式进行训练,并通过决定系数(R2)、均方根误差(RMSE)和平均绝对误差(MAE)进行比较。决策树回归表现最佳(R2 = 0.9945),其次是线性回归(R2 = 0.9908)、随机森林(R2 = 0.9892)、LSTM(R2 = 0.9731)和SimpleRNN(R2 = 0.9718),而KNN(R2 = 0.8038)和SVM/SVR(R2 = 0.1038,经过特征缩放)表现较差。这些结果在考虑了编码子使用的大规模组成约束、基于实例和边界回归器对未缩放、共线性小样本数据的敏感性,以及深度序列架构在非常小的表格样本伪序列上的有限优势后进行了评估。本文以透明的方式展示了流程结果、统计结果和比较建模结果,同时列出了数据集的局限性,为未来基于编码子组成的尼帕病毒计算研究提供了基准。

title: Geometrical study of DNA sequences of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus using the ATG genomic walk method
abstract: Viral genome analysis is essential for characterizing genetic variation and evolutionary patterns, while complementary computational approaches may provide additional insights beyond conventional sequence-based methods. In this paper, the complete RNAs of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus are analyzed using a DNA walk method that traces the distribution of ATG triplets along sequences. It provides visual one-dimensional models (ATG trajectories) of genomes on a plane and quantitative estimates based on: (i) point-defined relative values of the divergence of ATG trajectories, (ii) relative global-defined standard deviation of ATG triplet numbers in a studied set of sequences, and (iii) relative global-defined standard deviation of fractal dimension values of inter-ATG distances in the same sequence set. These calculated parameters for the two species mentioned are compared with those of previously studied viruses, allowing them to be arranged in the following order based on their increasing sensitivity to variations in ATG distribution: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus, Nipah, Ebola, and dengue viruses, which is in good accordance with their observed and recognized mutability. The method verified in this paper can be used as a supplementary pre-screening qualitative and quantitative tool for conventional sequencing analysis.

It provides visual one-dimensional models (ATG trajectories) of genomes on a plane and quantitative estimates based on: (i) point-defined relative values of the divergence of ATG trajectories, (ii) relative global-defined standard deviation of ATG triplet numbers in a studied set of sequences, and (iii) relative global-defined standard deviation of fractal dimension values of inter-ATG distances in the same sequence set. These calculated parameters for the two species mentioned are compared with those of previously studied viruses, allowing them to be arranged in the following order based on their increasing sensitivity to variations in ATG distribution: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus, Nipah, Ebola, and dengue viruses, which is in good accordance with their observed and recognized mutability. The method verified in this paper can be used as a supplementary pre-screening qualitative and quantitative tool for conventional sequencing analysis.

title: Temporal Fusion of RT-qPCR and IgM/IgG Serology for Nipah Virus Diagnosis: A Critical Narrative Review and a Proposed Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework
abstract: Nipah virus infection is a high-consequence zoonosis of South and South-East Asia for which laboratory confirmation rests on two assay families whose informativeness moves in opposite directions across the course of illness. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction performs best while viral nucleic acid remains detectable in blood and the oropharynx, whereas enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays for immunoglobulin M and immunoglobulin G become informative as nucleic acid disappears. Prevailing practice interprets these assays as independent dichotomous results obtained at a single moment, discarding quantitative magnitude, specimen provenance and the day of illness on which each specimen was taken. This review critically evaluates whether the longitudinal structure of the two assay families can be exploited jointly, and what explainable artificial intelligence would need to deliver before such a model could be used in outbreak conditions. Human clinical studies describing the temporal behaviour of molecular and serological markers were appraised alongside the methodological literature on diagnostic accuracy without an adequate reference standard, and the computational literature on temporal and multimodal fusion and on explanation methods in clinical decision support. The evidence consistently indicates an ordered transition in which clearance of viral nucleic acid from blood precedes the appearance of virus-specific immunoglobulin G, and that the combination of detectable viraemia with absent immunoglobulin G at presentation carries adverse prognostic weight. Confidence in these observations is nevertheless constrained by very small samples, over-representation of the minority who survive, the absence of an international nucleic-acid standard, and geographical concentration of evidence in Bangladesh and Kerala. No clinical prediction model that fuses molecular and serological results over time was identified for this infection. A conceptual dynamic framework is developed that separates established temporal relationships from hypothesised gains, specifies the evaluation and governance requirements that would apply, and identifies prospective serial-sampling cohorts as the rate-limiting evidential step rather than model architecture.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the diagnostic challenges of Nipah virus infection, a high-consequence zoonosis in South and South-East Asia, by evaluating the potential of integrating longitudinal data from molecular and serological assays. The study contributes to the development of improved diagnostic strategies for Nipah virus, particularly in outbreak settings, but the findings are not yet sufficient to support clinical implementation without further validation.

title_zh: RT-qPCR和IgM/IgG 血清学在诊断中的时间融合:关键叙述性综述及可解释人工智能框架的提出
source_body_en: Nipah virus infection is a high-consequence zoonosis of South and South-East Asia for which laboratory confirmation rests on two assay families whose informativeness moves in opposite directions across the course of illness. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction performs best while viral nucleic acid remains detectable in blood and the oropharynx, whereas enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays for immunoglobulin M and immunoglobulin G become informative as nucleic acid disappears. Prevailing practice interprets these assays as independent dichotomous results obtained at a single moment, discarding quantitative magnitude, specimen provenance and the day of illness on which each specimen was taken. This review critically evaluates whether the longitudinal structure of the two assay families can be exploited jointly, and what explainable artificial intelligence would need to deliver before such a model could be used in outbreak conditions. Human clinical studies describing the temporal behaviour of molecular and serological markers were appraised alongside the methodological literature on diagnostic accuracy without an adequate reference standard, and the computational literature on temporal and multimodal fusion and on explanation methods in clinical decision support. The evidence consistently indicates an ordered transition in which clearance of viral nucleic acid from blood precedes the appearance of virus-specific immunoglobulin G, and that the combination of detectable viraemia with absent immunoglobulin G at presentation carries adverse prognostic weight. Confidence in these observations is nevertheless constrained by very small samples, over-representation of the minority who survive, the absence of an international nucleic-acid standard, and geographical concentration of evidence in Bangladesh and Kerala. No clinical prediction model that fuses molecular and serological results over time was identified for this infection. A conceptual dynamic framework is developed that separates established temporal relationships from hypothesised gains, specifies the evaluation and governance requirements that would apply, and identifies prospective serial-sampling cohorts as the rate-limiting evidential step rather than model architecture.
abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒感染是一种在南亚和东南亚地区具有高后果性的人兽共患病,其实验室确诊依赖于两个检测方法家族,它们在疾病过程中提供相反方向的信息。逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)在病毒核酸仍能在血液和咽部检测到时表现最佳,而免疫球蛋白M和免疫球蛋白G的酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)则在核酸消失后变得具有信息量。目前的实践将这些检测视为在单一时间点获得的独立二元结果,忽略了定量数值、样本来源以及每个样本采集时的疾病天数。本综述批判性地评估了这两种检测方法家族的纵向结构是否可以联合利用,并探讨了在暴发条件下使用此类模型之前,可解释人工智能需要提供哪些要素。同时,评估了描述分子和血清学标志物时间行为的人类临床研究,以及在缺乏充分参考标准的情况下关于诊断准确性的方法学文献,以及关于时间与多模态融合和临床决策支持中解释方法的计算文献。证据一致表明,在尼帕病毒感染中存在一个有序的过渡过程,其中病毒核酸从血液中的清除先于病毒特异性免疫球蛋白G的出现,且在初次就诊时检测到病毒血症而免疫球蛋白G缺失的组合具有不良预后意义。然而,这些观察结果的信心仍受到样本量非常小、幸存者过度代表、缺乏国际核酸标准以及证据地理集中于孟加拉国和喀拉拉邦等因素的限制。未发现针对该感染的临床预测模型,该模型能够随时间融合分子和血清学结果。为此,提出了一种概念性的动态框架,该框架区分了已建立的时间关系和假设的收益,明确了适用的评估和治理要求,并确定了前瞻性连续采样队列研究作为证据的关键限制步骤,而非模型架构。

title: Awareness of Nursing Students About Nipah Virus Infection: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to determine the awareness of nursing students regarding Nipah virus infection. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 72 nursing students from a public sector nursing college. Data were gathered pertaining to their knowledge of the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, complications, and prevention of Nipah virus infection using a structured questionnaire. Data were analysed using SPSS version 27.0. Descriptive statistics were used. The normality of the data was assessed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests. Owing to the non-normality of the data, the chi-square test was applied to determine the association between categorical variables. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.Results: The mean age of the participants was 21.6 ± 0.54 years. Of the 72 nursing students, 62.5% of the students had heard about Nipah virus, while 63.9% correctly identified it as a viral infection. About 80.6% knew about its transmission to others. 52.8% were adequately aware of the natural reservoirs of Nipah virus. Most (68.1%) students identified encephalitis as a significant complication. Preventive measures like avoiding partially eaten fruits (73.6%), using personal protective equipment (83.3%), hand hygiene (76.4%), and isolation of cases (84.7%) were broadly acknowledged. Most (61.1%) received information about this deadly virus from social media. Significant associations were observed between age groups and knowledge of the natural reservoir (P < 0.05) and isolation from cases as a preventive practice (P < 0.02). Conclusion: Nursing students had moderate awareness of Nipah virus infection. Social media played a pivotal role in knowledge acquisition about the Nipah virus. Keywords: Nipah virus, nursing students, encephalitis, natural reservoir, social media.

analysis.study_design_and_population: An in silico study was conducted to screen compounds derived from Tinospora cordifolia for their potential to block Nipah virus fusion, focusing on molecular interactions without involving experimental testing on biological systems.
analysis.methods: The research utilized computational methods to analyze the molecular structure of Tinospora cordifolia compounds and their potential interaction with Nipah virus fusion proteins, based on existing literature and databases.
analysis.main_results: The study identified several synthetic small molecules from Tinospora cordifolia that showed potential for inhibiting Nipah virus fusion, though no experimental validation was provided.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Tinospora cordifolia may contain compounds with antiviral potential against Nipah virus, offering a novel direction for drug discovery in the context of viral fusion inhibition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform future research into natural products for antiviral development, potentially contributing to the surveillance and treatment strategies for Nipah virus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in silico data without experimental verification, resulting in moderate confidence in the proposed antiviral activity of the identified compounds.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of synthetic small molecules from Tinospora cordifolia to inhibit Nipah virus fusion through in silico analysis. The research is motivated by the need for effective antiviral agents against Nipah virus, which is a significant emerging pathogen. The methods involve computational screening of compounds based on molecular interactions with the virus. The main results suggest several compounds may have antiviral potential, though no experimental validation was conducted. The interpretation highlights the novelty of using Tinospora cordifolia as a source for antiviral drug discovery. The findings could inform future research into natural products for antiviral development, particularly in the context of Nipah virus infections. However, the study's reliance on in silico data without experimental verification limits the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

title: TransmiRisk-AI: an agentic AI-based risk assessment framework for zoonotic diseases using integrated surveillance data
abstract: Introduction Zoonotic disease outbreaks are increasing in frequency and complexity, highlighting the need for intelligent surveillance systems capable of real-time monitoring and risk assessment. Existing surveillance approaches are often reactive, fragmented, and dependent on manual analysis, limiting timely public health responses. Methods This study presents TransmiRisk-AI, an agentic AI-driven surveillance framework designed to support automated zoonotic disease risk monitoring and decision-making. The framework integrates a hybrid risk scoring model with a multi-agent architecture comprising data ingestion, risk assessment, alert generation, execution, logging, and orchestration agents. These agents collaboratively automate data collection, preprocessing, risk evaluation, outbreak monitoring, and alert dissemination. To enhance situational awareness, the system incorporates outbreak intelligence from WHO Disease Outbreak News and dynamically updates disease risk profiles based on outbreak recency, frequency, and severity. An interactive Streamlit dashboard provides transparent visualization of risk categories, outbreak trends, and system activities. Results Case studies involving the Nipah virus and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever demonstrate the framework's ability to adapt to evolving epidemiological conditions. Discussion TransmiRisk-AI offers a scalable and interpretable digital health solution that supports proactive surveillance and timely decision-making within a One Health context.
